tier_reason: README 'Performance Overview' gives first-party db_bench results vs RocksDB v6.12 with CPU/DRAM/SSD stated, but the numbers are only in a table image (docs/images/compare_rocksdb.png) and exact db_bench command lines, engine options, compiler and flags are not given, so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table image compare_rocksdb.png (db_bench, TerarkDB vs RocksDB v6.12): QPS heavy_read 695.2K vs 398.1K (~1.75x), heavy_write 215.6K vs 127.1K (~1.70x), fillrandom 204.4K vs 118.8K (~1.72x), fillseq 215.7K vs 208.4K (~1.04x) (ratios derived from page data); P99 read latency heavy_write 73.10us vs 573.68us, P99 write latency heavy_write 75.81us vs 1,029.90us
corrections.workload: db_bench with 10 client threads, 20GB requests/thread, 24-byte keys and 2000-byte values; 'heavy_read' (90% read), 'heavy_write' (90% write), fillrandom and fillseq.
corrections.caveats: TerarkDB is itself forked from RocksDB v5.18.3 but benchmarked against a newer RocksDB v6.12 (different vintages); results appear only as a table image (compare_rocksdb.png), not in text; exact db_bench command lines, engine options (e.g. whether TerarkZipTable was enabled), compiler and flags are unstated; fillseq gain is only ~1.04x. Latest default-branch commit (2026-05-31) is a README update; last code change 2025-08-25.

notes: The 'graph' is actually a numeric table image; claimed_speedup rewritten with its QPS and P99 figures (ratios marked derived). last_commit corrected from pushed_at (2026-07-13, another branch) to the default branch dev.1.4 head; still active. tier_reason: First-party PingCAP blog (Apr 25, 2019) states 70% higher write and 180% higher update performance vs RocksDB with CPU/RAM/disk and dataset described, but benchmark configs, compiler and flags are not published, so it is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: About 70% higher than RocksDB in data-loading (write) scenarios, with the gap growing as value size increases, and 180% higher in update scenarios; also better point-query performance, but underperforms RocksDB on range queries and has slightly higher space amplification
corrections.workload: go-ycsb against TiKV in transaction mode, TiKV-on-Titan vs TiKV-on-RocksDB; 64GB raw dataset with TiKV memory capped at 32GB via cgroup; 16-byte keys, 1KB values (64M keys) and 16KB values (4M keys); data loading, update, point-query, range-iteration and output-size tests.
corrections.caveats: First-party vendor (PingCAP) blog from 2019 rather than an independent or peer-reviewed source; measured end-to-end through TiKV (writes go through the Raft log first, which the post says dilutes Titan's gain), not Titan vs RocksDB standalone; go-ycsb configs, versions, compiler and flags not stated; percentages read from charts/text with no raw tables.
